title: Integer factorization

problem.name: Integer factorization
problem.statement_latex: Given an odd composite integer $N$ in binary, output primes $p_i$ and positive integers $e_i$ such that $N=\prod_i p_i^{e_i}$. Write $n=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$. The balanced semiprime case underlies RSA. The explicit-integer comparison uses quantum gate complexity and classical bit complexity.
problem.statement_text: Given an odd composite integer $N$ in binary, output primes $p_i$ and positive integers $e_i$ such that $N=\prod_i p_i^{e_i}$. Write $n=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$. The balanced semiprime case underlies RSA. The explicit-integer comparison uses quantum gate complexity and classical bit complexity.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n^2)$ total gates, Shor and Regev factoring.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(n^2)$ total gates, Shor and Regev factoring.
quantum.details_latex: Shor's order-finding algorithm uses $\widetilde O(n^3)$ gates with elementary arithmetic and $\widetilde O(n^2)$ with fast arithmetic; its logical space is $O(n)$. Regev uses $\widetilde O(n^{3/2})$ gates per circuit and $\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+4$ repetitions, followed by polynomial-time lattice postprocessing. The total quantum gate count is $\widetilde O(n^2)$, with shorter individual coherent computations. Pilatte establishes unconditional correctness for the recent factoring framework.

classical.headline_latex: $L_N[1/3,(64/9)^{1/3}]$ heuristic time, general number field sieve.
classical.headline_text: $L_N[1/3,(64/9)^{1/3}]$ heuristic time, general number field sieve.
classical.details_latex: Here $L_N[\alpha,c]=\exp((c+o(1))(\log N)^\alpha(\log\log N)^{1-\alpha})$. This is the standard fastest heuristic comparator for general balanced RSA semiprimes. It includes smooth-relation collection and sparse linear algebra. Rudich--Rousseau also announce deterministic worst-case $N^{o(1)}=2^{o(n)}$ time using the Boolean tensor-contraction theorem. That result specifies a deterministic guarantee; its $o(n)$ exponent does not quantitatively rank it against heuristic GNFS.

strength.description_latex: Subexponential to polynomial in the input bit length, through Fourier sampling.
strength.description_text: Subexponential to polynomial in the input bit length, through Fourier sampling.

evidence.description_latex: Strong evidence under the standard assumption that factoring is classically hard in polynomial time. The algorithms give upper bounds in the explicit-integer model.
evidence.description_text: Strong evidence under the standard assumption that factoring is classically hard in polynomial time. The algorithms give upper bounds in the explicit-integer model.

hardware.description_latex: Small factoring circuits have been demonstrated. RSA-sized instances require fault tolerance and polynomial arithmetic workspace. Gidney's RSA-2048 estimate uses about 1,409 logical qubits and projects fewer than one million physical qubits and an approximately one-week runtime under the specified architecture assumptions.
